Page also says 'Check your mailbox storage to see what's taking up space.', 'If a message has an attachment larger than 25 MB, Outlook cannot send the message.', and 'If an error occurs, remove the signature from the email and re-send.'

Exact page sentence differs from the excerpt. Page says: 'If you can't sign in to your account, use the Microsoft account sign-in helper.' Also on page: 'update your password if it's been changed recently', 'Your account might also be temporarily blocked because we noticed some unusual sign-in activity.', and the link text 'Learn how to unblock your Outlook.com account'.

required_actions.action: Check mailbox storage to see what is using space
If storage and mailbox are not full, check the account
If the password was changed recently, update it
If the account may be temporarily blocked, use the unblock article linked on the Microsoft page

findings: Step 2 ('If your storage and mailbox aren't full, check your account. If your password was changed recently, update it.') combines two separate actions in one step.

Step 3 ('If the account may be temporarily blocked ... follow the linked article ... If you can't sign in, use the Microsoft account sign-in helper.') combines two conditional actions in one step, and 'the linked article' names no article the user can find.
correction_required: Replace steps 2 and 3 with: '2. If your storage and mailbox aren't full, check your account.' '3. If your password was changed recently, update it.' '4. If your account may be temporarily blocked because of unusual sign-in activity, follow the link 'Learn how to unblock your Outlook.com account' on the Microsoft support page.' '5. If you can't sign in, use the **Microsoft account sign-in helper**.' Keep steps 1, 4 and 5 of the current target as steps 1, 6 and 7 (renumbered): step 1 'Check your mailbox storage to see what's using space.', step 6 'Attachments over 25 MB can't be sent.', step 7 'If a signature causes an error, remove it and resend.'

source_checks.finding: Verbatim excerpt confirmed: 'Sometimes power cycling your printer can resolve the issue.' Page confirms: 'If you are using a Windows 11 device, start by running the automated printer troubleshooter in the Get Help app.' and 'Turn off your printer and unplug it, wait 30 seconds, plug your printer back in, and then turn the printer back on.'

The writer's excerpt repeats the power-cycle sentence and is not the connection text. Page says: 'Make sure that the printer's USB cable is properly connected from the printer to your PC.' It does not say 'firmly'. Page also says: 'If your printer's status displays "Printer in error state," there may be a problem with the printer itself.' and 'check the printer for low paper or ink, and be sure the cover isn't open and the paper isn't jammed.'

required_actions.action: Open the printer troubleshooter in the Get Help app
Power cycle the printer: turn it off, unplug it, wait about 30 seconds, plug it back in, and turn it on
Re-check that the USB cable is properly connected (user already said it is plugged in)
If the status reads 'Printer in error state', check for low paper or ink, an open cover, or a paper jam

findings: Step 3 says the USB cable is 'firmly connected'. The page says the cable is 'properly connected from the printer to your PC' and never uses 'firmly'.
Step 2 says only 'wait', dropping the 30-second wait that both the passage and the page give; the user cannot tell how long to wait.
correction_required: Step 3 becomes: '3. Confirm the **USB** cable is properly connected from the printer to the PC.' Step 2 becomes: '2. Power off the printer, disconnect it, wait about 30 seconds, reconnect it, and power it on.'
